title: Finite intrinsic inverse-image direct-image adjunction
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $f:X\to Y$ a scheme morphism. Use intrinsic inverse image [def-sp-finite-intrinsic-pullback] and the actual constant-coefficient module direct image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Transport the fixed-scalar inverse-image/direct-image adjunction through the canonical realization equivalences, then conjugate its right adjoint by the direct-image comparison uniquely fixed to be identity on constant-scalar unit sections. This defines the existing sfIntrinsicConstantModuleAdjunction. Its right-derived adjunction uses the specified K-injective direct image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and its derived realization comparison is the localization of that same section-normalized map on K-injective representatives.

proof.text: Write E_T for fixed-scalar module sheaves embedded in module presheaves, and U_T for restriction along the constant-scalar unit. The module sheafification adjunction gives E_T ≅ realization_T followed by U_T: its unit is invertible because the underlying abelian presheaf is already a sheaf. U_T is fully faithful, since the module sheafification counit is invertible. The canonical coefficient direct-image map composed with the scalar unit is the scalar unit at the base-changed object, by the defining sheafification hom-equivalence.

Restricting intrinsic direct image along constant scalars gives the fixed-scalar direct image of the restricted module: use the identity on every section, with linearity given by the scalar square of step 1. Compose this identity with the inverse source realization unit and the target realization unit. Full faithfulness of U_Y lifts the resulting natural isomorphism uniquely. On a source scalar-unit section, the inverse source unit cancels the source unit, giving exactly the target scalar-unit section. Conversely these source units are isomorphisms on sections, so agreement on all such sections implies equality of the components and of the natural isomorphism.

For the derived square, write L and R for source and target realization, H for fixed-scalar direct image and G for intrinsic direct image. The equivalence L preserves K-injectives, being right adjoint to its exact inverse. On complexes form two natural transformations from Q(LG(-)): the first is the unit of RG after L, followed by the inverse exact-localization comparison for L; the second is Q of the section-normalized comparison from step 2, followed by the inverse exact-localization comparison for R and R applied to the unit of RH. Both are isomorphisms on K-injectives. Their quotient therefore prescribes the desired isomorphism on every K-injective representative.

Every derived object is isomorphic to QI for a K-injective I. Every derived morphism between such representatives is Q of a complex morphism, after passing through the homotopy category, by the K-injective Hom bijection and surjectivity of the homotopy quotient. Naturality of the two units in step 3 therefore gives naturality on all derived morphisms between representatives. Conjugate the representative components by chosen isomorphisms X ≅ QI to extend to a natural isomorphism. Naturality proves its prescribed value on every QI independently of the choice. Cancelling the two invertible units rewrites its equation as the published normalization. That equation fixes every component on QI; naturality along X ≅ QI fixes all remaining components, proving uniqueness. The existing definitions select the uniquely specified comparisons and transport the fixed-scalar adjunction unchanged.

def sfIntrinsicConstantModuleAdjunction
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A] :
    sfIntrinsicPullback A f ⊣ proEtaleConstantModuleDirectImage f A
